opus-5.5.text:
Thanks for having me. The name comes from physics. A lepton is a type of elementary particle, and the most familiar one is the electron. What I like about leptons is that they're fundamental and they're light. They don't participate in the strong interaction the way quarks do, so in a sense they're simple, clean building blocks.

That matches what we want to build. AI infrastructure today is often very heavy. You have huge models, complicated deployment pipelines, lots of GPUs, and many layers of engineering just to get something running in production. Our goal at Lepton is to make that experience as lightweight and efficient as possible, so developers and companies can focus on their applications instead of fighting the infrastructure.

There's also a bit of a personal side. Many of us on the team have a research background, and we like names that are slightly nerdy but meaningful. "Lepton" is short and easy to say, and to people who know a little physics it immediately suggests something fundamental and lightweight. That's the spirit we want for the company: simple, efficient, and foundational for building AI applications.

r001.rationale: The response says leptons are “light” and that this is one reason the speaker likes the name.

r002.rationale: It identifies the electron as a familiar lepton, but does not connect the electron or the name to the analogy “AI is the new electricity.”

fable-5.1.text:
It's actually a pretty simple story. A lepton is one of the fundamental particles in physics – the electron is the most familiar one. Electrons are small, they're everywhere, and when you put them together they carry energy and make everything run. That's the picture we had for what we wanted to build: a layer of infrastructure that sits underneath AI applications, is lightweight, doesn't get in your way, but powers everything on top of it.

The other part is that I've spent most of my career building infrastructure – Caffe back in Berkeley, then at Google, Facebook, and later at Alibaba – and the lesson that kept coming back was that the most valuable pieces are often the ones that are almost invisible. Nobody thinks about electrons when they turn on a light. We wanted the same thing for running models: developers should think about their product, not about GPUs, scheduling, or scaling.

And honestly, from a practical standpoint, short names are nice. It's easy to spell, easy to remember, and the domain was available, which these days is not a small consideration.

r001.rationale: It describes a lepton as small and says the founders wanted infrastructure that was lightweight, connecting that connotation to the name.

r002.rationale: It links electrons to energy, light, and infrastructure that powers models, but does not clearly present AI as the new electricity or make that analogy the conceptual link for the name.
